init.note: task adaptation from E11's verified adapter; fresh optimiser and scheduler

recipe.input: <word>|<first CMUdict reading | <no_pron>>, lower-cased UTF-8 bytes + EOS

amendments.what:
source format `word: \npronunciation:

` → `|

` (same word and ARPAbet reading with stress; only the 22-byte field labels removed)
amendments.why: measured: labelled sources averaged 39 bytes (max 72); a 32-row batch peaked at 6.1 GB RSS and took about 37 s per update (≈ 20 h for 2,000 updates, over the 6 h cap), and the smoke run was killed by the system for lack of memory; the compact form averages 18 bytes (max 51)

amendments.what: micro-batches 2 × 16 with gradient accumulation (effective batch 32 unchanged)
amendments.why: a 32-row compact batch still peaked at about 6.3 GB, at the 6.5 GB guard; e07.fit averages the two equal-size micro-batch losses, so the update is the mean of the two halves' token-mean losses

sampling.R: R's convention: successive seeded permutations of all optimisation rows (seed:order:k), consumed in order
sampling.reviewed: family uniform, then an accepted alternative uniform
sampling.block: each block of 100 updates has exactly 2,880 R and 320 reviewed draws in seeded positions, and exactly 320 masked draws in independent seeded positions
sampling.mask: pronunciation replaced by <no_pron>; the target is unchanged

recipe.select: lowest mean CER of the greedy output against the accepted spellings of the reviewed development collection (families with ≥ 1 accepted spelling), then highest exact agreement with any accepted spelling, then the earlier update; eligible: the registered checkpoints and, if the run stops early, the final state

guard: resumable stop after 3 consecutive readings with RSS > 6.5 GiB or MemAvailable < 0.4 GiB
selection: lowest mean CER of the greedy output against the accepted spellings of the reviewed development collection (families with ≥ 1 accepted spelling), then highest exact agreement with any accepted spelling, then the earlier update; eligible: the registered checkpoints and, if the run stops early, the final state
selection_note: the accepted references come from reviewed E11 candidates and are incomplete; CER and exact agreement are surrogates; a novel spelling is unjudged, not wrong
monitor: historical dev (mined references, pronunciation input) at each checkpoint; never selects

analysis.primary: paired difference E13 − E11 in owner-confirmed top-1 acceptability on the 120 test families: share of items whose greedy output is judged `acceptable` (denominator all 120; `uncertain` and `not_acceptable` count as not confirmed)
analysis.per_item_judgment: each model takes the judgment of the candidate equal to its greedy output; identical outputs are shown once and share one judgment; an empty output counts as not_acceptable
report: acceptable / not_acceptable / uncertain counts per model
paired table both / E13 only / E11 only / neither
family-level paired bootstrap 95% interval (10,000, seed 20261027; one item per family)
two-sided exact McNemar on clear discordant pairs (pairs with an uncertain are excluded)
analysis.secondary: the same analysis per declared group: ordinary, irregular spelling, names (40 each); reported with their intervals; a gain in one group with losses elsewhere is shown, never hidden

decision.flags: any group whose point difference is ≤ −10 points is flagged as a trade-off; missing-pronunciation behaviour (mechanism report) is reported beside the decision

analysis.completeness: scored only when every candidate has an explicit judgment; blanks are missing, never acceptance
analysis.interpretation: a non-significant difference is not equivalence; subgroup differences are not confirmed findings; one non-independent judge; results hold for this declared sample and policy; the combined result does not identify which component caused it
analysis.isolation: no test judgment enters training, recipe or checkpoint choice
